identity.name: Early Dynastic Period of Egypt
alt_names: First and Second Dynasties of Egypt

land.text: the Nile valley and Delta from the First Cataract to the sea, 'the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt in c. 3150 BC'

predecessors.note: The page says the period 'lasting from the end of the archaeological culture of Naqada III'. The Naqada culture dossier (another group) ends in -3000 on Cliopatria's date; this dossier starts at the page's c. 3150 BC, so the two overlap for 150 years.

land.text: the same Nile valley and Delta: 'until c. 2686 BC, or the beginning of the Old Kingdom'

successors.note: Same land, Third Dynasty (Djoser) onward; the Old Kingdom page gives 'Began: c. 2686 BC'.

capitals.name: Memphis (Ineb-Hedj; Mit Rahina)
capitals.note: Page: 'With the First Dynasty, the Egyptian capital moved from Thinis to Memphis.' Thinis (near Abydos, exact site unlocated) was the earlier capital and the rulers' hometown; no year is given for the move, so it is tied to the start of the First Dynasty at the period's start.

correction.text: the Nile valley and Delta as in Cliopatria's first Early Dynastic shape, held from the unification 'in c. 3150 BC' instead of from -3000

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the row in -3000, but the page dates the period from 'the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt in c. 3150 BC' and calls the process gradual (possibly a few centuries). Shape unchanged, years extended back 150 years.

93,286 km2 for the Nile valley and Delta from Elephantine (lat 24.0) to the coast (31.6). The page gives no infobox area; the Old Kingdom page's 'the Nile River region south to Abu (also known as Elephantine)' agrees with the southern edge. The page's undated, hedged sentence that the state 'had likely imposed its authority as far north as modern Tel Aviv and as far south as the second cataract in Nubia' is not drawn (see notes).

correction.text: unchanged shape; years cut to end at c. 2686 BC, the end of the period, with the later years -2685..-2501 belonging to the Old Kingdom

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria runs this shape to -2501, but the page ends the period 'until c. 2686 BC, or the beginning of the Old Kingdom' (infobox c. 2690) and the Old Kingdom page begins 'c. 2686 BC'. The identical shape is used by the Old Kingdom dossier from -2686. Shape unchanged.

region.text: Upper and Lower Egypt, the Nile valley from Elephantine to the Delta

ledger.note: c. 3150 BC: Upper and Lower Egypt are united and the Early Dynastic Period begins. Page: 'the era of ancient Egypt that immediately follows the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt in c. 3150 BC'; it describes the unification as a gradual process over perhaps a few centuries (a paraphrase, no date). The page names the two lands, not a boundary, hence 2.

With the First Dynasty the capital moves from Thinis to Memphis: 'With the First Dynasty, the Egyptian capital moved from Thinis to Memphis.' The page gives no year; it is tied to the First Dynasty, which the period 'is generally taken to include' from its start.

region.text: the Nile valley and Delta, passing to the Old Kingdom

ledger.note: c. 2686 BC: the Early Dynastic Period gives way to the Old Kingdom. Page: the period lasts 'until c. 2686 BC, or the beginning of the Old Kingdom'; the Old Kingdom page reads 'Began: c. 2686 BC' and Djoser (Third Dynasty) as its first king.

wars.name: Unification of Upper and Lower Egypt
wars.outcome: The page mentions 'a campaign to conquer Lower Egypt and the Nile Delta' (Narmer/Menes) and dates the unification to c. 3150 BC; no year or battle for the campaign itself.
wars.note: Not dated beyond the period start. The same page says 'Warfare between Upper and Lower Egypt occurred often' and gives Peribsen's seal ('He of Ombos has joined the Two Lands for his son, the Dual King Peribsen', dated ca. 2660-2650 BC, 'at the end of the Second Dynasty'); no dates or lands for any single episode, so no contest is drawn.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders; the state is the Nile valley and Delta, bounded by desert and by Elephantine in the south.

sources.title: Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)
sources.note: Identity, c. 3150-c. 2686 BC, capital move from Thinis to Memphis, Peribsen seal, hedged extent to Tel Aviv and the second cataract.

sources.title: Old Kingdom of Egypt
sources.note: Successor: 'Began: c. 2686 BC'; southern edge at Elephantine; area check.

notes: Cliopatria's two rows of this state (-3000..-2701, -2700..-2501) are one identical shape of 93,286 km2. Dates: the page gives c. 3150-c. 2686 BC (infobox c. 2690); Cliopatria gives -3000..-2501 and the Old Kingdom from -2500, so this dossier starts 150 years earlier and ends 185 years earlier, and the Old Kingdom dossier takes the shape from -2686. SEAM FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: the Naqada culture dossier (another group) ends in -3000, so the Naqada culture and this state overlap -3150..-3000 on the same land; one of the two dates needs reconciling. NOT DRAWN: the page's sentence that 'the Egyptian state had likely imposed its authority as far north as modern Tel Aviv and as far south as the second cataract in Nubia' (undated, hedged) and 'Egyptian settlement and colonization ... from about 3200 BC onward all over the area of southern Canaan' (Tell es-Sakan inhabited 3300 to 3000 BC); these precede or straddle the start and give no year for a border, so southern Canaan and Lower Nubia stay outside the shape. The page's Peribsen date (ca. 2660-2650 BC) lies after its own period end of c. 2686, so the page is internally inconsistent; no event rests on it. The page lists no dynasty dates and no king list; no ruler strip is given. Thinis is not in the gazetteer (needed only if a later agent draws the earlier capital). Early Dynastic, Old Kingdom, First Intermediate, Middle Kingdom are Cliopatria's periods of one continuous Egyptian state; they share family 'egypt'.
